Maintenance Report — MNT-0059-006

Asset: WELL-0059 (SW-24 Well 059, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 23 Dec 2023 08:00 · Finished: 02 Jan 2024 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 233 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0059-0062 on 2023-12-21 Report written: 03 Jan 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0059-0062 showed the wellhead at 17.7 °C with the air at 12.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0059-006 (WS-06).

The thermal reading at inspection INS-0059-0066 showed the wellhead at 20.6 °C with the air at 11.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Maintenance Report — MNT-0059-009

Asset: WELL-0059 (SW-24 Well 059, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 22 Mar 2024 08:00 · Finished: 27 Mar 2024 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 132 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0059-0075 on 2024-03-21 Report written: 27 Mar 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0059-0075 showed the wellhead at 22.1 °C with the air at 19.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 4 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.action: Replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0059-013

Asset: WELL-0059 (SW-24 Well 059, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 04 Oct 2024 08:00 · Finished: 05 Oct 2024 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 20 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0059-0102 on 2024-10-03 Report written: 06 Oct 2024

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0059-0102 at 08:45 on 2024-10-03 found crude oil on the pad: about 0.9% of the pad area, estimated 0.2 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.6 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 282 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 226 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 0.5 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0059-013 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.87% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).
